text: 🇲🇽✊ Mexican inflation drops to 3.94% — below the 4% target for the first time this year. "Yesterday inflation dropped. We're under 4 percent... 3.94, under 4 percent, inflation keeps falling." — Claudia Sheinbaum, June 10 mañanera Sheinbaum tied the result to the PACIC pact with producers, fuel-price stabilization (gasoline and diesel held flat), direct work with tomato growers, and the public Centrales de Abasto. Tools the neoliberal playbook said could not work.

🇲🇽🏭 Mercado Libre: $4.6 billion into Mexico in 2026 — biggest annual investment in the company's history here. "It's the result of confidence in Mexico. If there were no confidence in Mexico, the peso wouldn't be where it is." — Claudia Sheinbaum, on the announcement $4.6B — 35% over last year. 8,500 new jobs, bringing the company to 42,000 employees in Mexico. Impact in 19 states. Announced the same day inflation dropped to 3.94% — first time below 4% this year.

🇲🇽🌎 The US barred Iran's World Cup team from staying overnight. Mexico stepped in. "Mexico is always willing to help all the peoples of the world." — Claudia Sheinbaum, on hosting Iran's team in Tijuana The US blocked Iran's full delegation from staying on its soil for the 2026 World Cup. FIFA called Mexico. Sheinbaum opened Tijuana — Xolos lent their facilities, Baja California cleared the way, the team will commute to its US matches from Mexican soil. World Cup kicks off June 11.

🇲🇽🛢️ <u>PEMEX HITS 5 CONSECUTIVE QUARTERS OF STABLE OIL PRODUCTION UNDER NEW DIRECTOR — CRUDE FEEDING MEXICAN REFINERIES</u>

Juan Carlos Carpio Fragoso — Pemex's new director, UNAM economist with a CIDE public-management master's — reported five straight quarters of stable crude output and a 2% rise in liquid hydrocarbons from February 2025 through April 2026.

The strategic fields are feeding the refineries the crude they need — exactly the integrated chain neoliberal privatizers spent two decades trying to dismantle.

Carpio: "Pemex's priority is to strengthen operational efficiency and cost optimization."

The financial press writes "world's most indebted oil company" in every headline. The reality is the Mexican state still owns and runs its own energy — and that's the variable Wall Street can't price. (Vía El Financiero)

🚨🇲🇽 <u>US CONGRESS APPROVES $70 BILLION FOR ICE AND BORDER PATROL — ON A 214-212 KNIFE-EDGE VOTE</u>

The House passed $70 billion for migration enforcement on a 214-212 razor margin: $38 billion for ICE, $26 billion for Border Patrol, $5 billion in unallocated "unexpected expenses" — money runs through fiscal 2029.

This stacks on top of roughly $140 billion Congress greenlit for immigration repression last year. Speaker Mike Johnson called it "a great triumph for Republicans."

The same House refuses to fund Medicaid expansion, extend universal child tax credits, or treat housing as a right. Cages over care — every budget cycle, the empire shows you exactly what it values.

Eight of every ten dollars in that $70 billion will reach Mexican families: in raids, in deportations, in detention beds, in dead bodies in the desert.

🇲🇽🏫 <u>SEP TO CNTE: 1,100+ TEACHERS REINSTATED, PRIMARY SALARIES MORE THAN DOUBLED — RETURN TO CLASSROOMS</u>

SEP Secretary Mario Delgado laid out the offer: under Sheinbaum, base primary teacher pay rose from 9,580 pesos in the Calderón era to over 20,000 today. More than 1,100 teachers fired for opposing Peña Nieto's 2013 neoliberal education reform have been reinstated.

The government has offered to scrap Usicamm — the evaluation regime CNTE has fought since 2013 — and rebuild the state-teaching relationship from scratch with labor protections.

Delgado: "Let's protect ourselves from falling into the practices that existed under neoliberal governments — nepotism, favoritism, sale of teaching posts."

Active strikes remain in Chiapas, Guerrero, Michoacán, Oaxaca, and Zacatecas. The 2007 ISSSTE pension fight isn't closed. But the gap between this offer and what PAN-PRI ever put on the table is structural.

🚨🌍 <u>EBOLA BUNDIBUGYO STRAIN: 93 DEAD, 534 CASES IN DRC AND UGANDA — WHO LAUNCHES $518M RESPONSE</u>

WHO confirmed Saturday June 6: the Bundibugyo strain outbreak across the Democratic Republic of Congo and Uganda has reached 93 dead and 534 confirmed cases. Risk classified "very high" inside DRC, "high" regionally, low globally.

The continental response — a $518 million plan from African health authorities and WHO — has to operate inside a humanitarian catastrophe: 15 million Congolese already need aid, 3.4 million of them displaced inside infection zones.

Decades of Western extractivism, war financing, and forced displacement built the kindling. Then the outbreak hits, and the empire's press calls it a "natural" disaster.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>TRUCKERS AND FARMERS DISTANCE THEMSELVES FROM JUNE 11 "PROTESTS" — SALINAS PLIEGO COUP NARRATIVE COLLAPSING</u>

The supposed national mobilization tomorrow at the World Cup opening just lost its base. National Trucker Association leader David Estévez: "We're not suicidal — we will not make the stew better for a group trying to ride on a just struggle."

The National Front for the Rescue of Mexican Agriculture also pulled out, citing ongoing dialogue with Gobernación.

Salinas Pliego's TV Azteca had been amplifying calls for chaos to coincide with FIFA's opening — Sheinbaum named it directly yesterday. Without truckers blocking roads and farmers in the streets, the "Mexico in chaos" montage has no actors left.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>NUEVO LEÓN HIDES POOR NEIGHBORHOODS WITH WALLS AND MESH FOR WORLD CUP</u>

Samuel García's government built 200-meter concrete walls and green cyclonic mesh along Boulevard Miguel de la Madrid and avenues Constitución and Morones Prieto — directly in front of Monterrey neighborhoods with sheet-metal and wood homes. Over those walls, FIFA welcome banners in Swedish and Korean.

The state human rights commission issued a formal warning June 8 demanding the government stop "invisibilizing" the Plaza of the Disappeared, where 7,000+ missing-persons faces were also covered with planters.

The Cup is one month. Those families live there 365 days a year.

REUTERS: "From cartel prison to children's playground: the transformation of Mexican World Cup host Monterrey"
June 9, 2026 | 🟡

📰 Reuters writes a fair piece about Monterrey's 15-year safety turnaround — quoting only Mexican residents, no parachuted US analyst — then slaps "From cartel prison to children's playground" on top. 🔍 The headline does what the body refuses to.

A reminder: clickbait framing exists even when the reporter delivers an honest story.

• Francisco Rodríguez, 66: "It's an enormous change."
• Activist Gala Rojas on Liberty Park: "When I was a child, I had nowhere to play."
